title: The Tiv put under the Jukun, and a Sarkin Makurdi
text: The British split the Tiv into three and kept them under outside rulers: the Jukun minority in the north-east, Cross River in the south and Lafia Division in the north-west. In 1914 they went as far as appointing Audu Dan Afoda, a Hausa-speaking Nupe Muslim who had served them as interpreter and political agent, as Sarkin Makurdi, “king of Makurdi”, and in 1927 made him head of the Tiv council. These arrangements failed, and in 1946 the Tiv chose their own Tor Tiv.
note: The years of the arrangement are approximate; the sources give the period, not dates.
reviewNotes: Spelling corrected from “Afoba” to “Afoda”, as in Ochonu (2008) and the Wikipedia Makurdi and Tor Tiv articles.
